answer:
Keep the direct link if it is useful for querying, but stop letting it be the whole record. In CRMarchaeo the direct find-to-context link already exists as AP21 contains (is contained in), domain A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit, range E18 Physical Thing — and the model itself declares AP21 to be a shortcut for the fuller path E18 Physical Thing → AP18i is embedded → A7 Embedding → AP19 is embedding in → A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit. That is the crux of your question. A shortcut in the CRM is not false; it is a weaker statement that stands in for a path with intermediate nodes (Introduction > Applied Form > Shortcuts). AP21 asserts only 'this object was inside that volume'. It has no slot for when the object got there, who observed it there, or how the excavator reads that presence. So the shortcut does not misrepresent the axe by saying something wrong; it misrepresents it by being the only thing said, which lets a reader infer that find date = context date.

The fix is to instantiate the path the shortcut stands for, and hang the residuality on the node it creates.

1. The axe fragment: E22 Human-Made Object.

2. The colluvial deposit — what your database calls the context: A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit. (AP19's range is A2 specifically, so the deposit, not an interface, is what the embedding sits in.)

3. Interpose an A7 Embedding: one instance per find, standing for the position of that find in that matrix.
   - A7 AP18 is embedding of → the axe (E22)
   - A7 AP19 is embedding in → the deposit (A2)
   - A7 AP17 is found by → the recovery event (S19)
   - A7 P2 has type → a term from your own vocabulary, e.g. 'residual / secondary deposition' (as opposed to 'primary' or 'intrusive')
   This is not an exotic construct reserved for finds whose embedding matrix was itself analysed. Martin Doerr told the SIG in 2022 that A7 had been 'interpreted wrongly in an overspecialized manner' and is meant 'for every position determination of a find within a layer' (t1592, Issue 585). And the SIG has repeatedly held that finds themselves are objects embedded in stratigraphic units rather than stratigraphic units in their own right ('finds are described as objects embedded in' Stratigraphic Units — Martin Doerr, t1123).

4. The recovery: S19 Encounter Event, with O19 encountered object → the axe, O21 encountered at → the find spot (E53 Place, i.e. your three-dimensional record), P4 has time-span and P14 carried out by for the excavation date and the recorder. The scope note of S19 is written around precisely your problem: it says that in archaeology there is particular interest in whether an object is found in situ, i.e. whether its embedding in the surrounding matter supports the assumption that it has not moved since the archaeologically relevant deposition event. For this axe the embedding does not support that assumption, and the A7 typed as residual is where you record that judgement.

5. Give the axe and the deposit separate chronologies, and relate them explicitly rather than by adjacency:
   - E12 Production, P108 has produced → the axe, P4 has time-span → Neolithic. This is what dates the object, and it is what your database currently has no field for.
   - A4 Stratigraphic Genesis, AP7 produced → the deposit, P4 has time-span → post-Roman. This is what dates the layer.
   - A4 P12 occurred in the presence of → the axe. This is the distinction between residual and intrusive: the axe was already in the sediment that accumulated, rather than working its way down into a layer that already existed.
   - The residuality claim itself: E12 (production of the axe) P183 ends before the start of A4 (genesis of the deposit). P183 is one of the temporal relation primitives the CRM added for exactly this kind of reasoning — the specification notes that sciences dealing with the past derive temporal topological relations from stratigraphic and other observations (Introduction to the basic concepts > Specific Modelling Constructs > Temporal Relation Primitives based on fuzzy boundaries).

With that in place, keep AP21 as well if your query layer wants a flat 'everything from context 1004' index: it is entailed by the full path, so nothing is lost and the two do not contradict each other. What changes is that the axe no longer borrows the layer's date by default, and the residual reading is an assertion someone made about a specific embedding rather than an absence in the data.

One honest limit: CRMarchaeo gives you no class or property that means 'residual'. The term has to come from your own vocabulary via P2 has type on the A7 Embedding, and the chronological claim has to be made explicit with P183. Nothing in the tools showed the SIG discussing residuality or the transport of a find into a later deposit under that name, so this is an application of the general machinery rather than a documented pattern.

rejected_alternatives.option: AP21 contains, used on its own (the current practice)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Not wrong, but it is declared in CRMarchaeo as a shortcut for the path through AP18i / A7 Embedding / AP19, and a shortcut carries no intermediate node. There is nowhere to attach the type of the embedding, the encounter that observed it, or a date. Keep it as a derived link, do not let it be the only link.

rejected_alternatives.option: A8 Stratigraphic Unit (or A2) for the axe itself
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Modelling the find as a stratigraphic unit was raised on the list and rejected: van Leusen answered that a find should not normally be modelled as a stratigraphic unit because 'the latter is intended to represent chronologically separable processes' such as cutting and filling (t1123). A bulk-deposited object is not a separable stratigraphic process.

rejected_alternatives.option: P46 is composed of / P56 bears feature, from the deposit to the axe
rejected_alternatives.why_not: AP18 is already a subproperty of P46, so the generic property adds nothing and loses the archaeological reading. P56 bears feature is for features attached to an object, not for an object lying inside a sediment body.

rejected_alternatives.option: E9 Move for the colluvial transport of the axe from upslope
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E9 Move is a subclass of E7 Activity, which the CRM defines as actions intentionally carried out by an actor. Downslope erosion has no actor. The arrival of the axe in this deposit is better carried by A4 Stratigraphic Genesis with P12 occurred in the presence of the axe; if you have evidence for the eroding source, model that upslope event separately.

rejected_alternatives.option: S5 Inference Making (CRMsci) or an E13 Attribute Assignment to reify the residuality judgement
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Defensible if you need the interpretation attributable to a named analyst and revisable, and the SIG does treat stratigraphic ordering as inferred (the 46th meeting decided that in the AP13 example 'earlier' must be made explicit as an inferred relation). But at the granularity this case asks about, P2 has type on the A7 Embedding plus the P183 statement records the reading without adding a third layer. Add it only if your archive needs competing interpretations side by side.

Correct and worth recording for the dig as a whole, but it is the removal of the matter, not the relationship between the axe and the layer. It does not bear on whether the direct link misrepresents the find, so I have left it out rather than pad the model.

siblings_considered.why_not: E25 Human-Made Feature is for features purposely created and physically attached to the site — the right class for the corn-drying oven, not for the axe. The axe's whole problem is that it is a detachable, transportable object, which is what allows it to be residual; making it a feature would assert it belongs where it lies.

A3 Stratigraphic Interface is a boundary surface, the limit of the effect of a genesis event. The colluvium is a body of matter with volume and an interior in which things sit; and AP19 is embedding in has A2 as its declared range, so an interface could not host the embedding.

A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit is the sibling the shortcut invites you to collapse into, and it is exactly what you have now: the surrounding matrix as a whole. It answers 'which layer' but has no per-find identity, so it cannot be typed 'residual', cannot be tied to the S19 that observed this axe, and cannot distinguish this find from every other object in the same context. I use A2 as well, for the matrix — but not instead of the embedding.

S23 Position Determination is what your total station does — it yields coordinates for the find spot and can be recorded as part of the recovery. But it determines a position; it does not record that a physical thing of interest was encountered in surrounding matter, which is the observation the in-situ question turns on, and AP17 is found by has S19 as its declared range.

E81 Transformation is tempting because the axe is broken: one could say the whole axe ceased to exist and a fragment came into being. I deliberately do not, because that would give the fragment a beginning of existence at the moment of breakage and cut it loose from the Neolithic production date that is the entire basis of the residuality claim. Keep one E22 with one E12 in the Neolithic, and record the breakage separately if it matters.

E12 Production is the other subclass of S17 Physical Genesis, and it is wrong for a colluvial deposit: E12 is for activities designed to, and succeeding in, creating new items. Colluvium accumulates through erosion and downslope wash with no design. A4 Stratigraphic Genesis is CRMarchaeo's class for the stratification-forming process, and AP7 produced is what attaches it to the deposit. (I do use E12 — for the making of the axe — which is the point: the two timelines are different kinds of event.)

notes: Two friction points. (1) `concept <id>` prints an explicit Siblings block only for CRMbase classes; for CRMarchaeo and CRMsci classes (A7, A2, S19, A4) there is no such block, so I derived siblings from the parent's 'Superclass of' line — A8 is superclass of A7, A2, A3; S27 is superclass of S4, S19, S21, S23; S17 is superclass of E12 and A4. (2) `quote` only accepts thread, message and document-chunk ids, so scope notes returned by `concept` (S19's in-situ passage, AP21's shortcut declaration) cannot be verified through it; I have described those in my own words rather than quoting them, though both are quoted almost verbatim in the concept dossiers. Also worth flagging: `ontology` lists only the 241 CRMbase identifiers and `docs` indexes only v7.3.2, so the whole of CRMarchaeo is reachable only by guessing identifiers at `concept`. A1 through A10 and AP1 through AP28 are current; A11, A12, AP9, AP14 and AP20 are not. Finally, I found no SIG discussion of residual or intrusive finds by name, so the chronological half of this answer is assembled from general machinery (E12 vs A4 time-spans, P183) rather than from a documented CRMarchaeo pattern.
